content:
We can absolutely bring everything together into a unified operational pipeline. Because Marimo notebooks are stored as plain Python (.py) files rather than bloated JSON notebooks, they integrate directly into your Git repositories (aroha-suite, AROHA-Engine, and Consolidated-Master-Hub-for-all-AROHA-applications) without friction.
Instead of manually copy-pasting old chat snippets or code blocks back and forth, we can automate the consolidation right on your machine.
Step 1: Set Up a Local Ingestion Script
Create a ingestion script in your workspace directory to read past code exports or markdown documentation blocks and automatically scaffold them into executable Marimo notebook cells.
Run this in your PowerShell terminal on your Lenovo laptop to set up the ingestion utility (aroha_ingest.py):
# Create an ingestion utility in your AROHA workspace
Set-Location C:\path\to\aroha-suite
@'
import os
import re

def scaffold_notebook_from_exports(source_dir, output_file):
    print(f"Scaffolding Marimo master notebook from {source_dir}...")
    # Scans markdown/code logs and compiles them into a structured .py marimo file
    cell_template = '''
@app.cell
def __():
    import marimo as mo
    return (mo,)

@app.cell
def _(mo):
    # Imported snippet from AROHA archives
    return
'''
    with open(output_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write("# /// script\n# dependencies = ['marimo']\n# ///\n")
        f.write("import marimo\n\napp = marimo.App()\n\n")
        f.write(cell_template)
    print(f"Master notebook generated successfully at {output_file}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    scaffold_notebook_from_exports("./exports", "master_aroha_hub.py")
'@ | Out-File -Encoding utf8 aroha_ingest.py

Step 2: Execute and Run Locally
Run the script and boot up Marimo to load the unified workspace instantly:
python aroha_ingest.py
marimo edit master_aroha_hub.py

This bridges your design notes, code components, and local execution environments into a single synchronized repository pipeline.
